title: At Comic-Con 2013 with David Choe and Asa Akira
summary: DVDASA's first live show is recorded at San Diego Comic-Con amid severe microphone problems, crowd overlap and visually dependent bits. David Choe, Asa Akira, Bobby NAMBLA, Money Mark and Critter interact with costumed fans, test Ask Asa, distribute stickers and prints, and run audience trivia. A recurring opening joke speculates about pedophiles in the crowd. It is neither a census nor an allegation against identifiable attendees; child-related language must not become a discovery surface. The central event is a medically and ethically reckless giveaway: an audience member called Edgar is encouraged to lick an open lesion on Bobby's hand, nicknamed Persephone, for a print. The cast openly says they are not clinicians, speculates incorrectly about warts, HPV and HIV, and later learns the participant brushed his teeth. The archive preserves what occurred without endorsing it and does not identify or contact the audience member. The relevant lesson is direct: do not expose another person to an undiagnosed lesion, and do not use this comedy as medical guidance. A second audience segment debates transgender sex using dated slurs and reductive claims. One speaker briefly objects to casual slur use, but the substitute term and 'third gender' framing are also historically incomplete. Metadata uses respectful modern language while retaining source wording in the transcript. Ask Asa covers bacterial vaginosis, douching, anal preparation, sexual preferences and performer identity. Several medical claims and hydrogen-peroxide/douching suggestions are unreliable and potentially harmful. A particularly important consent failure appears when speakers say a man who answers no to anal contact secretly likes it; another participant explicitly asks, 'what about asking?' The archive rejects the no-means-yes generalization and retains direct communication as the safe interpretation. Later advice about bargaining for sexual acts, sitting on a sleeping partner's face, or using pornography to manipulate desire is joke/advice in the source, not consent. An audience participant and Asa voluntarily touch nipples while cameras are present; the moment does not authorize republishing private photographs or constructing an erotic excerpt. The show also captures fan culture: Thumbs Up costumes, a Choe-bot contest winner dressed as Critter, handmade props, a self-described pornography reviewer, merchandise prompts and trivia callbacks. Private fans receive pseudonymous treatment even when first names are spoken onstage. The episode ends with the public cast sign-off, though the ASR again corrupts David Choe and Asa Akira's names.
source_notes: The single automatic cleaner edit removes an empty record; all meaningful corrections are human-authored.

Audience first names and descriptions are performance context, not permission to build identity profiles.

No held-out acoustic speaker validation exists; line-level speakers remain unnamed.
speaker_policy: Public stage metadata may name David Choe, Asa Akira, Bobby NAMBLA, Money Mark and Critter Fleming. Audience members, partners and fans remain private or pseudonymous even when a first name is audible. Stage address and costume do not validate acoustic identity.
